extracted.intended_audience: students and practitioners of broadcast journalism (news writers, reporters, producers)
extracted.subtask_description: A comprehensive textbook-style guide covering skills, techniques, style, reporting, producing, ethics, and career preparation for broadcast journalists working in radio and television. It presents fundamentals plus contemporary examples and scripts with interviews of news professionals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduction
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefatory material setting out the book's purpose and approach to broadcast news writing, reporting, and producing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frames the text's examination of skills, techniques, and challenges; orients reader to the coverage of fundamentals and the use of real scripts and interviews as examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broadcast news writing mechanics
rubrics_metrics.description: Fundamental mechanical principles for writing news for broadcast media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers the basic nuts-and-bolts of constructing broadcast copy; placed early to establish technical foundations used throughout the book.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broadcast news writing style
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles and conventions that define effective broadcast news style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides guidance on stylistic expectations unique to broadcast (conciseness, clarity, spoken-word considerations); illustrated with examples and scripts.

rubrics_metrics.name: More style rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional stylistic rules supplementing the core broadcast writing style guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expanded rules and refinements beyond the main style chapter; intended to fine-tune writers' approach to broadcast copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing broadcast copy
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical instruction on composing broadcast copy for news segments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focuses on craft of turning information into usable copy for on-air delivery; examples and sample scripts used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color : the key to good writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of ‘color’ (vivid detail) as essential to engaging broadcast writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains why and how to add descriptive, vivid elements to make stories resonate for listeners/viewers while maintaining broadcast constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing for the radio newscast
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific techniques and considerations when writing copy for radio newscasts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses radio's unique demands (audio-only delivery, pacing, lead-ins) with examples and scripts tailored to radio practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing for the television newscast
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific techniques and considerations when writing copy for television newscasts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers interplay of visuals and words, pacing for TV, use of sound bites and on-screen elements; includes TV-specific script examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delivering the news
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on on-air delivery and presentation of news content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers vocal delivery, timing, presence, and how delivery interacts with written copy to convey journalistic intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finding the news
rubrics_metrics.description: Techniques and strategies for news gathering and story discovery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains sources, beats, story ideas, and methods to identify newsworthy events and angles; foundational to reporting assignments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broadcast news reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Core reporting practices tailored to broadcast journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses how to research, verify, structure, and report stories for broadcast formats, with examples and methodological guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting assignments
rubrics_metrics.description: How reporters approach, plan, and execute assigned stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical advice on assignment management, deadlines, shaping the story, and delivering usable material for newscasts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Covering planned events
rubrics_metrics.description: Techniques for covering scheduled news events effectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on preparation, logistics, story framing, and on-site reporting expectations for events such as press conferences, hearings, and ceremonies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting live
rubrics_metrics.description: Skills and considerations for live, on-the-scene reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focuses on immediacy, accuracy under pressure, coordination with production, and technical constraints of live broadcasts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Putting the television story together
rubrics_metrics.description: How to assemble the elements of a television story into a coherent on-air piece.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers scripting, visual selection, editing, sequencing, and integrating sound bites and graphics for TV storytelling.

rubrics_metrics.name: The interview
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles and techniques for conducting effective broadcast interviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes question design, preparation, on-air conduct, and tactics to elicit usable sound bites while preserving journalistic ethics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collecting information from documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Using public and private documents as sources for broadcast reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains methods for document research, verification, and turning documentary information into broadcast-appropriate content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computer -- assisted reporting for broadcast
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of computer-assisted reporting (data and digital tools) in broadcast journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses leveraging data, databases, and computer tools to develop and enhance broadcast stories; reflects contemporary reporting techniques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Developing sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Building and maintaining sources for ongoing broadcast reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers source cultivation, trust-building, and ethical considerations in using and protecting sources for news gathering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specialty reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on beats and specialized forms of reporting (e.g., investigative, science, business) in broadcast.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses how topic-specific expertise affects reporting approach, sourcing, and presentation in broadcast formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics and law
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal and ethical standards relevant to broadcast journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduces key legal constraints (libel, privacy, copyright) and ethical principles that govern broadcast practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: More ethical issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional ethical challenges and considerations beyond the core ethics chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expands on complex ethical dilemmas reporters and producers may face, with discussion and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tabloid journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Examination and critique of tabloid-style journalism and its relationship to broadcast news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses sensationalism, audience pressures, and the ethical/journalistic trade-offs of tabloid approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Producing
rubrics_metrics.description: The role and responsibilities of the news producer in broadcast operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers story selection, rundown construction, coordination between reporters and technical staff, and overall show management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using the hardware
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical instruction on broadcast equipment and technical tools used in news production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses cameras, audio gear, control-room equipment, and operational basics producers and reporters must understand.

rubrics_metrics.name: The job search in a changing industry
rubrics_metrics.description: Career guidance for entering and advancing in the evolving broadcast journalism industry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offers advice on job search strategies, adapting to industry changes, and skills employers seek in newsrooms.
